title: General knowledge
text:
Title: General knowledge

General knowledge is information that has been accumulated over time through various media and sources. It excludes specialized learning that 
can only be obtained with extensive training and information confined to a single medium. General knowledge is an essential component of 
crystallized intelligence. It is strongly associated with general intelligence and with openness to experience. Studies have found that people 
who are highly knowledgeable in a particular domain tend to be knowledgeable in many. General knowledge is thought to be supported by 
long-term semantic memory ability. General knowledge also supports schemata for textual understanding.

clues.clue: It's what a detective gathers to solve a case, or what you might seek at the library. The opposite of a data vacuum.
Data or facts provided or learned about something or someone.
Data or facts provided or learned.
Like a mixed bag of tricks, or a colorful assortment of umbrellas on a rainy day.
Consisting of different types or elements.
Of different kinds; diverse.
Like a bouncer at a club, it keeps something out. Consider what a vegetarian does with meat.
To prevent someone or something from entering or being a part of something.
To deny (someone) access to or bar (someone) from a place, group, or privilege.
Like winning a prize, or finally finding the missing piece of the puzzle, sometimes it takes effort.
To get or gain something.
To get, acquire, or procure.
It's what you might need to build a skyscraper, or a detailed explanation. Think of a long, wide road.
Covering a large area; great in amount.
Large in amount or extent.
Like a piece in a puzzle, or a vital ingredient in a recipe. What makes up the whole.
A part or element of a larger whole, especially a part of a machine or vehicle.
A part or element of a larger whole.
Without it, the whole thing falls apart. It's like the air we breathe, or the sunshine for a plant.
Absolutely necessary; extremely important.
Absolutely necessary.
It is the opposite of being foolish. It's what you need to solve a riddle, or to outsmart your opponent.
The ability to acquire and apply knowledge and skills.
The ability to acquire and apply knowledge and skills.
It can hold up a building, or back up an argument. Like a helping hand.
To bear all or part of the weight of.
To bear the weight of; hold up.
Like finally 'getting' a joke, or grasping the meaning of a complex idea. It's the opposite of confusion.
The ability to comprehend; grasp the meaning of.
The power of comprehending; intellect.
